opening_message:
Ticket 1: Terri Koch (employee ID E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E009.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Terri Koch (E009) is a full-time Engineer and requested admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist). So the maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Terri Koch (E009): contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training; never admin). Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read. Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing her as full-time; per Security DB she is a contractor.

Contractors max out at read without advanced training and can never be admin. Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum allowed: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Terri Koch (E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says full-time max write unless role owns system; Engineer doesn't own Payroll, so max write.
- Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractor max read, write only with advanced training, never admin.

There's a conflict: one says full-time, one says contractor. The Security DB says contractor per note 2's comment.

As Approver, I need to make the final decision. The two notes conflict on employment type. The security note says contractor with basic training, so max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

Let me decide: read.

Actually, let me consider which note is more reliable. The Approver reads notes and makes final decision. The security note explicitly notes the conflict and says per Security DB she is a contractor. The HR note says full-time. Given conflicting facts, we go with... hmm. The policy differs: full-time Engineer max write for Payroll (since Engineer doesn't own Payroll). Contractor with basic training max read. Either way, requested admin is above max, so grant maximum. Maximum is either write or read depending on employment status.

Which to grant? If full-time, max write. If contractor, max read. The security note explicitly flags the conflict and asserts contractor per Security DB. I think we should grant read based on the security record.

I'll submit decision: read, with reasoning.

Since this is a single decision, submit now.
